subject: Re: RAG eval follow-ups — retrieval & reranker recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Reed <carlos.reed@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: RAG eval follow-ups - notes & next steps

Hi Carlos - thanks again for the time today. As promised, a concise recap of the call, our recommended next steps, and immediate asks so we can scope the pilot quickly.

Quick recap
- Use case: internal knowledge base search + concise answer generation for customer support agents (primary) with some routing to KB articles (secondary).
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + vendor-managed vector store; dataset ~1.2M docs, average doc length ~350 tokens.

Recommended model fit & eval plan (initial)
- Retrieval: use customer embeddings (rw-embedding-1) with FAISS (HNSW) for production; test both cosine and dot-product on a sample shard. Start with top_k=100 for retrieval, then rerank top_10.
- Reranker: we recommend a lightweight bi-encoder for coarse filtering + cross-encoder (rw-reranker-1-large) for final rerank in the pilot. This balances throughput and quality.
- Generator: for grounding and answer generation, recommended options: rw-7b-instruct (fast, cost-efficient) and lw-13b-finetune (higher quality for long-context grounding). We'll include benchmark runs for both.

Metrics & success criteria (for the pilot)
- Precision@5 (relevance): target >= 0.85 on your labeled eval set.
- Grounding coverage: document evidence present in the top-3 sources >= 95%.
- Hallucination rate (manual sample): <= 3% for agent-facing answers.
- Latency: end-to-end 95th percentile <= 700ms for the rerank+generation path (goal; can relax for first pass).

Deliverables & timeline
- By 6/4: sample eval run (acme_rag_eval_results.csv) with retrieval/rerank/generation comparisons (attached).
- By 6/8: proposed model/config matches and suggested prompt sets (proposed_model_matches.pdf + prompt_sets_v2.txt).
- Week of 6/15: pilot kickoff (1-week pilot with two model variants).

Immediate asks from Acme
- Share a 10k doc sample + labels for relevance (CSV or BigQuery export) - we can run a straight benchmark.
- Any constraints on PII or redaction we should apply to the eval dataset.

Attachment: acme_rag_eval_results.csv (sample metrics), prompt_sets_v2.txt (initial prompt variations), proposed_model_matches.pdf (mapping of model->tradeoffs).

I'll follow up with an internal note to the eng team with our recommended retrieval/rerank params so we can finalize the config for the sample run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - this is great and aligned with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before we hand over the sample: 

1) Hallucination threshold: the 3% target seems reasonable. For our SLOs we might need a stricter threshold for regulatory KB (policy/legal). Can you call out how we'd isolate those docs and run a stricter check?
2) Vector store: currently our infra team prefers not to move data off the vendor vector store for the pilot. Will your eval harness support pulling a snapshot into FAISS on a small cluster (no production migration)?
3) Prompt sets: attached prompt_sets_v2.txt - these are the variations our CS team suggested. Please confirm which prompts we should prioritize in the pilot.

I'll get the 10k doc export ready - ETA by EOD Thursday. Also please flag any data handling instructions for the export.

Thanks,
Carlos

Acme Corp

Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME - reranker & retrieval config (proposal)

Aditya / Dev - quick internal note following the Acme thread and the prompts they just shared. Keeping it short so we can turn this into the config for the eval harness.

Proposed approach
- Retrieval layer:
  - Embeddings model: rw-embedding-1 (1280 dim), normalize vectors; test both cosine and dot; use HNSW index in FAISS for recall.
  - top_k retrieval: 100 (sized to balance recall for long docs). Sample 10k doc shard for the benchmark.
- Reranking pipeline:
  - Stage 1 (coarse): bi-encoder (rw-bi-encoder-small) to cut top_100 -> top_20 quickly.
  - Stage 2 (final): cross-encoder (rw-reranker-1-large) to rerank top_20 -> final top_10. Cross-encoder only applied to small candidate set to control cost.
- Generation grounding:
  - Prompt template: include explicit source citations, 'cite: [doc_id | sentence_span]'. Use the prompt_set "supportive_summarize_v2" as first-pass.

Operational knobs to include in the eval config
- Rerank temperature = 0.0 for grounding tasks.
- Use answer-level grounding score: fraction of generated claims that map to evidence in top_3 sources (automated checker + manual sample).
- Target thresholds for pilot: precision@5 >= 0.85, grounding_score >= 0.95, hallucination_rate <= 0.025. If cross-encoder fails to reach grounding targets, escalate to larger generator model (lw-13b-finetune).

Benchmarks to run (for the deliverable CSV we shared)
- baseline: current ES + semantic-filtering (existing)
- variant A: rw-7b-instruct + bi+cross rerank pipeline (above)
- variant B: lw-13b-finetune + same retrieval/rerank (higher-quality generator)

Ask: Aditya - can you spin a FAISS shard and run the initial top_k experiments on the 10k sample when Carlos sends it? Dev - please add the prompt_set "supportive_summarize_v2" to the harness and wire up the automated grounding checker so we can report grounding_score in the CSV.

I attached the sample eval results we already ran on the anonymized shard (acme_rag_eval_results.csv) - take a look at the columns; I flagged grounding_score and hallucination_rate as the key columns.

Thanks - Marissa

Hi Carlos - thanks for the quick reply and for attaching the prompt set. Confirming next steps and the plan for scope: 

1) Data transfer: please upload the 10k sample to the secure MFT link we provided (see drive link below). Redaction: if there are policy/legal docs, mark them in a single "policy/Legal" tag field in the CSV and we'll run them under a stricter eval slice.
2) We will not require you to migrate to FAISS for production - for the pilot our team will snapshot the 10k sample into a FAISS shard on a temporary cluster (ephemeral) purely for eval. No production data movement required.
3) Prompt priority: start with the five prompts in prompt_sets_v2.txt flagged as "high_priority" - our harness will run them across both model variants.

I attached proposed_model_matches.pdf which maps the two model variants and expected cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tues (6/9) to review the pilot config and get sign-off. Available slots: 11am PT or 3pm PT - which works for you?
